scope: Existing evidence supporting proposed CPU execution and initial Goldilocks/FRI proving experiments. No new build, test, profile or benchmark results.
source_status: Modified working tree; hashes cover the cited files only, not a complete reproducible prover build.

initial_prover.execution_scope: One execution per version; proof samples reuse that execution. No repeated-execution speedup is established.

word_streams.scope: Representation only: verifier channels deliver range-checked u32 words (hint kzg.io.read4) instead of bytes; parse cursor = (word list, byte offset 0..3); u32/32-byte fields read as words; key/claims/proof/policy hashed by a word-level BLAKE3 driver (16 words per block row, Blake3::compress_init unchanged); transcript keeps reversed word list + 0..3 tail bytes, fields absorbed 8 words per row; XOF over words. Transcript and digest bytes unchanged (Init proof accepted, digests match, pairing holds).

word_streams_and_grouping.scope: Historical packed BN steady-state count comparisons; not initial Goldilocks timings.
observations: I1 (split programs): first key 379,542 B / 43 circuits, steady key 399,566 B / 76 circuits (single combined key was 463,203 B). Steady-state verification 263.7M -> 213.9M padded (172.2M unpadded); stage 2 190.5M padded. Proof 158,673 B, 4,692 values, 70 points.

I2 (word streams) with the byte-era grouping regressed padded cells (steady 256.0M, stage 1 854.9M) although unpadded fell (steady 148.2M): 16 new ungrouped word circuits (92 total), KzgGroup_reuse crossing 2^17 rows, and KzgTranscript::observe_bytes (per-byte push in the per-column commitment absorption, 345K rows) inside the 289-wide KzgGroup_cold_b. Transcript/digest bytes unchanged: kzg-xof.ixa and kzg-source.ixa regenerate byte-identically to the streams experiment and every native/Aiur check passes.

I2 regrouped (i2q): steady key 440,350 B / 42 circuits, proof 115,689 B, 3,444 values, 60 points; steady verification 175.5M padded / 129.5M unpadded (max height 2^19); stage 1 636.0M padded / 499.9M unpadded. Adding many members to an existing wide group widens it (columns add up across members): the i2p variant that put them into cold_b/cold_c (cold_b 289 -> 510 wide) measured 215.4M.

I3 (sharding, copies in key): k<=2 gives steady 161.8M committed padded (129.6M unpadded verification, unchanged) and stage 1 607.5M; k<=3 with a column-only cost model added 2.7K values to every steady proof and raised unpadded verification to 167M (each extra copy also re-evaluates the circuit's constraint graph in the next verifier); with 600 cells/node added to the model, k<=3 keeps steady at 163.1M/129.4M, cuts stage 1 to 541.0M but makes stage 2 213.2M (bigger first-program proof). Sharding also absorbs row drift across a power of two (k3 stage 4: KzgGroup_reuse 131,072+256+128 instead of 262,144).

normalized_wrapper.scope: Target pipeline step 2, iteration 2: Init raw root -> normalized CompressWrap (grouping m16384w64, layout v2, FRI (2,100,0,20) unchanged) -> packed CompressGL on the wrap proof -> 3x CompressBNPacked::chain_v1 (CUDA). Raw-root and wrap chains run back to back on an idle machine with the same binary and BN artifact. Every proof verified natively; changed outputs rejected.
normalized_wrapper.grouping_finding: The grouping compiler gives a many-member group a wide union of columns (G_cold: 805 cols; even the <64-column members alone give 496). Rows, not widths, decide where they belong: m16384w64 keeps the 22 functions with 16k-65k Init rows in their own group (G_mid: 191+64 cols, 2^20) and splits the <=16k-row cold functions by width into a narrow group (409+44 cols, 2^18) and a wide one (367+130 cols, 2^16). Pure thresholds (t16384, s16384w48) cut wrap cells further but add ~600-900 opened columns, which costs CompressGL more than the wrap saves.

latest_compression_pipeline.scope: Starts from an already produced Init root; excludes initial ix prove.

research_limits: No measured word-stream execution speedup on IxVM or Goldilocks aggregation.
Cell counts do not establish elapsed-time improvements.
Source/layout changes require explicit new artifacts and key identities.
